newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos says to appeal against Manila Hotel ruling.
newsitem.headline: Ramos says to appeal against Manila Hotel ruling.

text.p: President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday he had instructed the government to request the Philippine Supreme Court reconsider its ruling preventing the sale of the Manila Hotel to a Malaysian firm.
Ramos told a news conference that the blocking of the sale could have serious repercussions on the country's privatisation programme.

The Supreme Court said on Monday the historic government-owned hotel was a national treasure and could not be sold to a foreign entity. It prevented the government from selling the property to Renong Berhad, which had won the 1995 bidding for the hotel, and instructed it to award the contract to the local Manila Prince Hotel Corp in keeping with a "Filipino First" policy.

"I have directed the Office of Government Corporate Counsels and the Office of Solicitor General to file a motion for reconsideration with the Supreme Court in view of the far-reaching effect on the court's decision and the government privatisation and deregulation projects," Ramos said.
Specifically, Ramos said he wanted a clarification on what constituted "national patrimony," the term used by the court to denote a national treasure.
He said this would guide future privatisation programmes.
"In the meantime, we are trying to formulate at the level of the executive, what we consider are a part of the national patrimony," he added.
On Tuesday, Ramos said he was "very disappointed" with the rulling, saying that foreign investments are crucial to the country's economic development.
